laura: Heads-up — EmberAI asked us to rework their Dedicated commit and safety margin for APAC (ap-northeast-1). They want predictable latency for Q3 launch and a squeezable buffer during marketing spikes. Can we sketch options?

marco: They said baseline traffic maps to ~40k GPU-hours/mo and could spike to ~70k during promotions. They want a 6–12 month committed term. Pricing push from them — looking for lower unit price if they lock-in more.

tina: Ok. Quick feasibility notes: ap-northeast-1 has limited spare capacity windows in our current fleet plan. To guarantee 70k peak w/ 99th%-ile latency targets we need either dedicated reserved slots or a reliable burst credit pool in another region with cross-region failover.

sanjay: Network note — cross-region fallback adds egress & latency. If they require <150ms p99 for inference, cross-region won't work for some workloads (esp. synchronous chat). We should quantify which endpoints can tolerate failover.

laura: EmberAI's product lead said only async embedding/rerank can tolerate failover; core chat must be local. They want at least 30 local GPUs guaranteed for chat lane, rest can be regional-burst.

tina: Rough conversion math I ran (A100-equivalent):
```
Baseline: 40,000 GPU-hours/mo ≈ 55 GPUs continuous
Peak: 70,000 GPU-hours/mo ≈ 96 GPUs continuous
Guaranteed local chat pool: 30 GPUs (24/7) = 21,600 GPU-hours/mo
Remaining baseline capacity to reserve: 40,000 - 21,600 = 18,400 GPU-hours/mo ≈ 25 GPUs
```
With those numbers, a commit of ~55 GPUs baseline + a 30% burst buffer would cover most spikes.

marco: They asked for safety margin options. We typically propose either: (A) headroom % on top of commit (e.g., +20% headroom baked into reserved price) or (B) separate burst credit bucket billed usage-first then reconciled. Pros/cons?

sanjay: Ops-wise, headroom is simpler for scheduling and SLAs — we keep the pool pinned. But it's more expensive for customer (pay for reserved even when idle). Burst credits are cheaper but risk contention. For ap-northeast-1 contention is realistic during holiday windows.

elliot: From CS perspective, EmberAI prefers predictable costs but is sensitive to upfront $/GPU. They've signaled willingness to trade a small price premium for lower outage risk. That suggests headroom approach might win.

laura: Proposed commercial options to send EmberAI: 
1) Conservative: Commit 60 GPUs baseline (≈43,200 GPU-hrs/mo) + 25% headroom = 75 GPUs reserved; higher monthly cost, full local SLA.
2) Hybrid: Commit 50 GPUs baseline (36k hrs) + 30 GPU burst credits (regionally pooled) — lower commit, cheaper unit price, but burst best-effort in busy windows.
3) Flexible: 12-month commit 55 GPUs + automated burst top-ups with negotiated max egress and a pre-paid burst credit tranche for peak months.

tina: Implementation caveats: if we do option 1 in ap-northeast-1 we must lock capacity now and schedule maintenance windows; deployment lead time ~6 weeks to reprovision GPUs and test runtime kernels for their model family. Option 2 requires cross-region routing rules + prefix KV cache warming strategy to avoid cold-start latency when failing over.

sanjay: Also add network & egress estimate: cross-region fallbacks add ~TB-level egress for embeddings-heavy tenants. Recommend we include an egress allowance in hybrid offers or explicit per-GB pricing cap.

marco: Can we surface a clear cost delta in the quote? Example quick calc: option 1 vs 2 monthly delta (rough):
```
Option1: 75 reserved GPUs * $X_gpu/mo = baseline_price1
Option2: 50 reserved GPUs * $X_gpu/mo + burst credits 30*peak_hours * $burst_rate = baseline_price2
Delta ~ 12–18% depending on X_gpu and burst_rate
```
We should fill X_gpu and burst_rate with seat pricing before sending.

laura: I'll draft the 3-option commercial and map the numbers to their usage profile. Tina/Sanjay, can you confirm technical feasibility and final lead times by EOD?

tina: Confirming — technical yes, lead time 6 weeks for local-only reserve, 3–4 weeks for hybrid (routing + burst).

sanjay: I'll produce an egress estimate and a short note on SLO implications (failover p99 impact) by EOD.

deploy-bot: Reminder — capacity-provisioning-run scheduled for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. If we decide on local reserved capacity, submit provisioning ticket before 2026-03-26. :bell:

laura: Great — will prep commercial and ping EmberAI with options tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
